1	\section{Introduction}
2	\label{sec:introduction}
3	
4	Temporal abstraction---enabling agents to reason and act at multiple time scales---has been a central aspiration in reinforcement learning since the options framework \citep{sutton1999options}. World-model RL offers a particularly compelling setting for this goal: a learned dynamics model can, in principle, imagine trajectories at variable temporal resolutions by conditioning on the step size $\dt$. This promise is concretely demonstrated by TAWM \citep{nhu2025tawm}, which conditions a world model on $\dt$ within the MPC framework of TD-MPC2 \citep{hansen2024tdmpc2} and shows consistent performance gains. A natural question follows: can the same $\dt$-conditioning bring temporal abstraction to imagination-based actor-critic methods such as DreamerV3 \citep{hafner2023dreamerv3}, where the policy and value function are trained entirely within imagined rollouts?
5	
6	We find that it cannot. Across every configuration we test, introducing variable-rate imagination into DreamerV3 degrades performance. Fixed $\dt{=}2$ imagination loses 86\% from peak return. Fixed $\dt{=}4$ never exceeds 19\% of the baseline. A learned gating mechanism with Gumbel-Softmax selection collapses to 11\% of baseline performance. These failures are not marginal---they are catastrophic, and they occur regardless of whether the temporal resolution is fixed or learned. The contrast with TAWM's success poses a sharp diagnostic question: why does $\dt$-conditioning succeed in MPC but fail in imagination-based actor-critic training?

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Temporal abstraction---enabling agents to reason and act at multiple time scales---has been a central aspiration in reinforcement learning since the options framework \citep{sutton1999options}. World-model RL offers a particularly compelling setting for this goal: a learned dynamics model can, in principle, imagine trajectories at variable temporal resolutions by conditioning on the step size $\dt$. This promise is concretely demonstrated by TAWM \citep{nhu2025tawm}, which conditions a world model on $\dt$ within the MPC framework of TD-MPC2 \citep{hansen2024tdmpc2} and shows consistent performance gains. A natural question follows: can the same $\dt$-conditioning bring temporal abstraction to imagination-based actor-critic methods such as DreamerV3 \citep{hafner2023dreamerv3}, where the policy and value function are trained entirely within imagined rollouts?

We find that it cannot. Across every configuration we test, introducing variable-rate imagination into DreamerV3 degrades performance. Fixed $\dt{=}2$ imagination loses 86\% from peak return. Fixed $\dt{=}4$ never exceeds 19\% of the baseline. A learned gating mechanism with Gumbel-Softmax selection collapses to 11\% of baseline performance. These failures are not marginal---they are catastrophic, and they occur regardless of whether the temporal resolution is fixed or learned. The contrast with TAWM's success poses a sharp diagnostic question: why does $\dt$-conditioning succeed in MPC but fail in imagination-based actor-critic training?

We answer this question through a systematic factorial analysis that isolates the causal factor: the \emph{trained} $\dt$-embedding. By contrasting trained embeddings against untrained (frozen random projection) and removed embeddings while holding all other factors constant, we identify a failure mode we term \emph{conditioning-induced value overestimation} (CIVO). The trained $\dt$-embedding enables the RSSM reward head to learn asymmetrically biased predictions across temporal scales---a $2.78\times$ gap in reward prediction error between $\dt{=}1$ and $\dt{=}2$---which the critic internalizes as optimistic value estimates. The normalized value-to-eval ratio ($\nve$) provides a clean diagnostic: a threshold of $\nve > 1.5\times$ achieves 4/4 separating power between trained and untrained embedding configurations. This mechanism is analogous to the delusional bias of \citet{lu2018nondelusional}, but arises from model imprecision amplified by learned temporal conditioning rather than policy-class constraints.

Beyond identifying the trigger, our analysis reveals three further findings that complicate the picture. First, the same CIVO trigger produces stochastic downstream outcomes across seeds---full collapse, self-correction, and oscillatory degradation---demonstrating that the vulnerability is deterministic but the damage is seed-dependent. Second, restricting imagination to $\dt{=}1$ while retaining the trained embedding does not prevent collapse: one of two seeds fails via a qualitatively distinct mechanism (evaluation-driven with increasing entropy, versus the value-driven decreasing-entropy signature of CIVO), revealing multiple vulnerability pathways. Third, the contrast with TAWM identifies the feedback architecture as the critical factor: $\dt$-conditioning succeeds when model errors are contained by re-planning from real states at every step, but fails when errors compound through the closed loop of imagination-based actor-critic bootstrapping.

We focus on DreamerV3 with the RSSM on Walker Walk from the DeepMind Control Suite \citep{tassa2018dmcontrol}, using multi-seed replication across all configurations to establish statistical robustness. Section~\ref{sec:related_work} situates our work in the temporal abstraction and value overestimation literatures; Section~\ref{sec:methodology} describes the factorial design and diagnostic metrics; Sections~\ref{sec:results}--\ref{sec:analysis} present findings and mechanistic analysis.

1	\section{Conclusion}
2	\label{sec:conclusion}
3	
4	We have presented a systematic factorial diagnostic of temporal abstraction in DreamerV3, identifying trained $\dt$-embedding as the causal factor behind conditioning-induced value overestimation (CIVO). The key findings are:
5	
6	\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
7	\item Every variable-rate imagination configuration degrades relative to the $\dt{=}1$ baseline, with degradation scaling monotonically with $\dt$.
8	\item Trained $\dt$-embedding reliably triggers pathological value overestimation ($\nve > 1.5\times$, 4/4 separating power), while untrained or removed embeddings prevent it.
9	\item The RSSM reward head develops a $2.78\times$ prediction gap between $\dt{=}1$ and $\dt{=}2$ under trained conditioning, providing the systematic bias that drives critic overestimation.
10	\item The same CIVO trigger produces stochastic downstream outcomes---full collapse, self-correction, and oscillatory degradation---across seeds of identical configurations.
11	\item Restricting imagination to $\dt{=}1$ does not fully prevent collapse: one of two seeds fails via a qualitatively distinct non-CIVO pathway (eval-driven with increasing entropy), demonstrating that the trained $\dt$-embedding creates vulnerability through multiple mechanisms.
12	\end{enumerate}
13
